```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`db2pq` resolves WRDS usernames from an explicit `wrds_id`, `WRDS_ID`,
`WRDS_USER`, and finally the keyring entry created by `wrds::wrds_set_credentials()`.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
Sys.setenv(WRDS_ID = "your_wrds_id")
wrds_get_username()
wrds_conninfo(format = "uri")
```

For reproducible PostgreSQL access, prefer libpq's `.pgpass` file where
possible. You can inspect whether a matching WRDS entry exists without opening a
database connection:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pgpass_has_entry(
  host = "wrds-pgdata.wharton.upenn.edu",
  port = 9737,
  database = "wrds",
  user = wrds_get_username()
)
```

Use `wrds_check_credentials()` to test a live connection when WRDS access is
available.
